messages:
julie: Hey team — POC with Acme. Their vendor security questionnaire has a BCP/DR section asking for RTO/RPO, backup cadence, failover topology, restore SLAs, DR test cadence, and whether backups are encrypted. Need a concise answer we can paste into the SIG/CAIQ doc for the vendor risk call in 2 hours.

sam: quick clarifying q: is this for Hosted Redwood API or Dedicated? The wording changes.

julie: Starting Hosted, likely dedicated later if they commit. For now they want Hosted details.

ryan: Notes from infra: For Hosted we have automated regional failover and health checks. Control plane failover typically completes in ~60–180s depending on DNS TTL and customer routing. Warm-pool customers see faster recovery. Our published Hosted SLA is 99.9%. RPO: persisted artifacts (configs, customer-uploaded models) are snapshotted; ephemeral runtime state (KV caches) is not persisted and therefore not covered by an RPO guarantee.

anya: Draft language suggestion to paste into questionnaire: short paragraph + bullets. High level facts to include:
- RTO: Control plane and routing failover targeted at 1–3 minutes; actual end-to-end visible recovery depends on DNS and client retries.
- RPO: Near-zero for persisted artifacts we manage; ephemeral caches are transient and not included. For Dedicated/Private, customers can opt into stronger replication guaranteeing lower RPO.
- Backups: Daily snapshots of customer artifacts and configuration with 30-day default retention; backups encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Failover: Multi-region passive-active routing with automated health checks and automated failover.
- SLA: Hosted API SLA 99.9% (paid plans); higher SLA options available for Dedicated under contract.
- DR testing: Quarterly DR exercises; runbooks and test evidence available under NDA.

ben: small infra clarifications for accuracy: control-plane re-route is ~60s; cold-starting GPU capacity can increase time-to-service for in-progress inferences — we use warm pools for critical customers to reduce that. Metrics/telemetry snapshots are hourly (7-day hot retention) and archived longer per contract.

sam: Can we also give a quick Q/A form for the SIG: Then include short answers like "Are backups encrypted? Yes (AES-256)." Keep it copy/paste friendly.

anya: I'll assemble one-paragraph canned answer + 6-line Q/A. Julie, want me to drop here for review?

julie: Yes please. Need it in 2 hours for their vendor risk call. Also they asked explicitly: 'Do you provide RPO guarantees for model state or customer-uploaded artifacts?'

ryan: Answer: For Hosted, persisted customer artifacts have near-zero RPO (snapshotted) but we don't promise RPO for ephemeral model runtime state (KV caches). For Dedicated customers we offer configurable synchronous replication options that can be contractually guaranteed.

anya: (10:35) Draft canned paragraph to paste into questionnaire:
"Redwood maintains documented business continuity and disaster recovery (BCP/DR) controls. For Hosted customers we maintain a 99.9% availability SLA and automated multi-region failover with typical failover reconciliation within 60–180 seconds depending on DNS propagation and customer configuration. Backups of customer artifacts and configuration are performed daily with 30-day default retention; all backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). RTO for control plane and routing actions is targeted at 1–3 minutes, and RPO for persisted artifacts we manage is near-zero. Ephemeral runtime caches (e.g., KV caches used during inference) are considered transient and are not covered by RPO guarantees. Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured for stronger RTO/RPO and custom replication/retention policies. DR exercises are performed quarterly and runbooks/test evidence are available under NDA."

anya: Quick Q/A bullets for SIG sheet: 
- Q: RTO? A: 1–3 minutes target for control plane failover (60–180s observed for Hosted).
- Q: RPO? A: Near-zero for persisted artifacts; transient caches not guaranteed.
- Q: Backup cadence? A: Daily snapshots (config/artifacts), hourly metrics snapshots.
- Q: Encryption? A: Backups encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+).
- Q: Failover topology? A: Multi-region passive-active with health checks and automated routing.
- Q: DR testing cadence? A: Quarterly; evidence available under NDA.

julie: LGTM — I'll paste into their questionnaire and flag the Dedicated follow-ups. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

dr-bot: DR test scheduled for next Friday 03:00 UTC (reminder set).
